name: Reuben Marsh
life: “I still remember checking my first railway coat in a tailor's window.” Thursday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Reuben asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I used that mirror to adjust my first work coat. I would gladly come to her house to do the same each anniversary.
appearance: Reuben has a high puff tied with plain cord, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. When somebody else has the floor, Reuben steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Reuben often says yes too quickly out of pride in being useful. The people closest to Reuben have learned to ask again the next morning, when the answer is more likely to account for sleep.
agenda: To return for one ordinary anniversary fitting.
family: Yusuf Bennett is Reuben’s cousin. Reuben asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Yusuf chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The other side of the cove*, Yusuf says, “I am the cleaner who came after her. A plaque can't promise working wages and I want both issues on the agenda.”
connections: Laurence Williams. A cautious family resemblance and an annual coat fitting both belong among the mirror's continuing uses.

reactions.situation: Another customer asks for a last fitting in front of it
reactions.response: Reuben sets aside an ordinary fitting time before making plans for the sale.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Reuben offers to cover one concrete expense and leaves the friend room to say the expense isn't the real problem.

reactions.situation: When two people ask for the same hour
reactions.response: Reuben rings both of them before quietly counting on somebody else to fill in.
